hook.line: Spanish emails get to the point in the first line: who you're writing to and why. One small frame does both jobs.
hook.es: Le escribo para confirmar la cita del jueves.
hook.en: I'm writing to confirm Thursday's appointment. (formal)

examples.es: Le escribo para pedirle información sobre el curso.
examples.en: I'm writing to ask you for information about the course. (formal)

examples.es: Te escribo para invitarte a almorzar.
examples.en: I'm writing to invite you to lunch. (to a friend)

examples.es: Les escribo para avisarles que el café cierra el lunes.
examples.en: I'm writing to let you know that the café is closed on Monday. (you all)

examples.es: Le escribo para agradecerle su comentario.
examples.en: I'm writing to thank you for your comment. (formal)

examples.es: Te escribo para darte las gracias.
examples.en: I'm writing to say thank you. (to a friend)

rule:
*Le escribo para* plus a verb: I'm writing to...

The first word says who's reading: *le* for *usted*, *te* for a friend, *les* for a group. The verb after *para* usually carries the same little word on its end: *pedirle*, *invitarte*, *avisarles*.

Keep the two matching. *Le escribo para pedirte* starts formal and slips into friendly halfway; Spanish readers notice.

English says I'm writing to, but Spanish uses *para*, never *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Le* or *Te* and type the whole sentence, writing to your friend Mariana: *___ escribo para invitarte a almorzar.*
yourTurn.answer: Te escribo para invitarte a almorzar.
yourTurn.why: Mariana is a friend, and *invitarte* already says *tú*, so *Te*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *pedirte* or *pedirle* and type the whole sentence, writing to a school you don't know: *Le escribo para ___ información sobre el curso.*
yourTurn.answer: Le escribo para pedirle información sobre el curso.
yourTurn.why: You started with *Le*, so the verb takes *le* too.

yourTurn.prompt: Start a formal email: I'm writing to confirm Saturday's reservation.
yourTurn.answer: Le escribo para confirmar la reserva del sábado.
yourTurn.why: Formal reader, so *Le escribo*; then *para* plus the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Write to a friend: I'm writing to say thank you.
yourTurn.answer: Te escribo para darte las gracias.
yourTurn.why: *Te* at the start, *darte* at the end: both friendly.

yourTurn.prompt: Write to the café's customers (you all): I'm writing to let you know that the café is closed on Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Les escribo para avisarles que el café cierra el lunes.
yourTurn.why: A group of readers gets *les* in both places.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal, writing to a man: *Te escribo para invitarte a almorzar.*
yourTurn.answer: Le escribo para invitarlo a almorzar.
yourTurn.why: For *usted*, *te* becomes *le*, and invite him is *invitarlo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: *Te escribo para preguntarte por el precio del arriendo.*
yourTurn.answer: Le escribo para preguntarle por el precio del arriendo.

pitfalls.why: Almost. You started with *usted*, so the verb takes *le* too.
I'm writing to is *para* in Spanish, never *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te escribo para invitarle a almorzar.
pitfalls.right: Te escribo para invitarte a almorzar.
pitfalls.why: *Te* means a friend, so the verb ends in *te* as well.
